subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Should OpenClaw ever suppress provider-visible tool-result content by global tool name, or should the DeepSeek cache fix be limited to a context-aware heartbeat/ephemeral-result policy?
rationale: This changes what the model can observe after tool calls, so code inspection can identify the current broad policy as unsafe but cannot choose the permanent cache/visibility contract alone.

options.title: Require a context-aware policy
options.body: Keep ordinary `exec`, `read`, `web`, and `memory` results visible and only summarize explicitly low-value heartbeat/status outputs or opt-in middleware paths with live proof.

options.title: Accept global summarization
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept that listed tools become model-visible placeholders everywhere, but that would be a significant behavior change for agent reasoning.

options.title: Defer to broader cache work
options.body: Pause this PR while the linked prompt-cache and tool-result visibility issues settle on one provider-cache policy.

recommendation.title: Require a context-aware policy
recommendation.body: Keep ordinary `exec`, `read`, `web`, and `memory` results visible and only summarize explicitly low-value heartbeat/status outputs or opt-in middleware paths with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest history signal for the prompt-cache/provider behavior and is listed for Agents ownership in CONTRIBUTING.md.
